answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, so a fresh identity starts near zero no matter how many clones a falcon-eyed attacker spawns. Each honest epoch raises the multiplier; a proven lie slashes it. Flooding an inlet with fake agents costs nothing but yields no influence, like water beside a river already flowing — aged honest accounts drown newcomers. The attacker pays real time plus collateral per identity, scaling linearly with desired influence and impossible to parallelize.
